title: After KvK1: what changes for an ordinary account
body_md:
**Who this is for.** Your kingdom has finished its first KvK and is heading into KvK2, KvK3 or a Season of Conquest (SoC) story. The daily routine of the base guide still applies; this guide covers what changes.

**The calendar.** Official notes set the first two Lost Kingdom seasons to **49 days** each, extended the Heroic Anthem SoC story to **50 days** (1.0.76) and cut the trip home after the Lost Kingdom from 3 to **2 days** (1.0.90) [B01-0900]. These are the officially stated lengths; current seasons may differ, so read your own event calendar. How long the gap between seasons lasts has **no official number**: one guide site gives two different figures (about 2 or about 3 months), and a kingdom that finishes an SoC story can register for the next one immediately [B01-0902, weak card].

**The pressure.** In its October 2024 Q&A Lilith itself said constant KvKs are stressful for players without time to gather between seasons, and announced a partial refund of healing resources at the end of KvK [B01-0901]. Plan the off-season as gathering and preparation time, not as a break.

**The three shifts after KvK1:**
1. **Troops:** T5 becomes a long research project, and healing (not training) becomes the main resource cost.
2. **Commanders:** the one-time Commander Swap and the Season 3 / SoC commander pools change what is worth building.
3. **SoC systems:** crystal technology, seasonal strategies and new currencies only exist inside SoC stories.
why_md: The KvK1 plan is about reaching CH21+ and T4 in about 100 days. After that the bottlenecks move to gold, healing and season-gated systems, and the cards for those stages are different, so a KvK1 checklist would point a KvK2 player at the wrong priorities.
uncertain_notes: B01-0902 (gap between seasons) is weak: one guide site with two inconsistent figures; no official count.

title: T5 is a research project measured in months
body_md:
**The gate.** Each T5 unit tech needs **Medical Corps 10**, **Academy 25** and the level-10 defence tech of its line (Royal Guard: Scutum; Royal Crossbowman: Pavise; Royal Knight: Plate Armor; Trebuchet: Heavy Frame). The T5 tech itself costs **10.0M food, 10.0M wood, 7.5M stone and 10.0M gold** and takes **100 days 1 hour** of raw research (Trebuchet 150d 1h) [A02-0600].

**Medical Corps** is the long pole: level 10 alone (needs Academy 24, Combined Arms 10 and Encampment 10) takes **231 days 14 hours** raw, and levels 1–10 together about **461 days** raw [A02-0600]. Raw times assume no research bonuses; with buffs they are shorter, but how much shorter is not measured (gap L-A02-05).

**Academy 25 needs Castle 25.** Buying the Books of Covenant with gems for Castle 24→25 alone is about **50,000 gems**, about 500 days of the F2P guaranteed gem income, so free accounts depend on books from barbarian forts [A04-0601, weak card].

**What to do:** start Medical Corps and the defence tech of your main line as soon as KvK1 ends, keep the Academy queue busy every day, and treat T5 as a goal for KvK3 or later rather than for KvK2 if you do not spend.
why_md: Players often plan T5 as the next step after T4. The research table says the gate is hundreds of raw research days, so the realistic question for a free account is which season, not which week. Starting the long techs early is the only lever a non-spender fully controls.
uncertain_notes: A04-0601 (gem price of Castle 25) is a derived figure from guide prices of Books of Covenant (weak card).

title: Keep T4 for the open field; use T5 where stats decide
body_md:
Guides agree that once you have T5, an account without a heavy gold economy should keep **T4 for large open-field fights** (cheaper heals, better trades) and use **T5 where stats decide the outcome**: rallies, garrison defence, 1v1 fights and Ark of Osiris (healed for free at the end) [A08-0606].

**Why gold is the problem.** In one guide site's healing calculator, healing a T5 infantry costs **20×** the gold of a T4 infantry (160 vs 8 gold per unit, before reductions) and about 2.7× the food and wood [A08-0603, weak card]. A seller guide quotes much larger absolute numbers that do not match the calculator, so do not plan with absolute heal costs from either source [A08-0604, contested].
why_md: Converting everything to T5 looks like progress on the power screen but can leave a free account unable to afford heals mid-KvK. Splitting by fight type follows the cost difference and is the advice the guide sources share.
uncertain_notes: A08-0603 (calculator constants, single guide site) is weak; A08-0604 is contested (seller site, numbers 6–9× the calculator). Only the T4/T5 role split (A08-0606) is firm.

title: Convert to T5 during scored events, and keep a T4 reserve
split_views: Same cost: a 2022 guide says T4 + upgrade = T5 trained directly. Higher cost: the wiki's Barracks page says upgrading has a greater overall resource cost [A08-0607].
body_md:
Guides advise converting troops to T5 **only during scored events** (Mightiest Governor training/power stages, Zenith of Power) with runes, kingdom buffs and titles active, and keeping a **T4 reserve** for field fights. In MGE a trained T5 is worth **100 points** vs **40** for a T4, and upgrades earn the point difference [A08-0607].

**Upgrade vs train is disputed.** One 2022 guide says T4 cost plus the upgrade cost equals training T5 directly; the wiki's Barracks page says upgrading costs **more** overall than training the higher tier directly [A08-0607]. Until this is measured (gap L-A08-07), upgrade only when the event points or the time saved justify it.
why_md: Training and upgrading happen anyway; doing them inside a scored event turns the same resources into event rewards. The cost dispute is real, so the block does not claim upgrading is free.

title: Healing is your main KvK cost: how wounds work and how to heal cheaply
body_md:
**What happens to wounded troops** [A08-0600]:
- Defending your own city, open-field and resource-point fights: severely wounded go to the **hospital**.
- Reinforcing an ally's city: **half** of your severely wounded die (official, 2025).
- Attacking cities or alliance buildings: **all** of your severely wounded die.
- Wounded that do not fit in the hospital **die**, so hospital capacity is a hard limit.
The sanctum, altar, shrine, pass and Lost Temple rows come only from a 2020 wiki revision; check them in-game before relying on them.

**Hospital capacity.** With all four hospitals at the same level, base capacity is **200,000** at level 21, **260,000** at level 24 and **300,000** at level 25 (level 25 needs Castle 25 and a Master's Blueprint) [A08-0605]. Research, alliance and item buffs add to this but were not quantified (gap L-A08-06).

**Heal in small batches.** Guides agree alliance help is the cheapest way to cut healing time: heal small batches (1–2k troops, or about 2-hour chunks) so helps finish them, avoid emptying the hospital with speedups mid-fight, and do not burn healing speedups outside meaningful fighting before a KvK [A04-0603].
why_md: Most KvK losses for ordinary accounts come from overflowing the hospital or healing everything with speedups at once. The wound rules decide which fights are cheap for you, and capacity decides how long you can stay in them.

title: Hall of Heroes: what comes back at the end of the season
body_md:
Official notes say troops in the **Hall of Heroes** are returned at the end of the season **even if you are offline** (1.0.45) [A08-0601, C04-0621]. Since **1.0.94** (May 2025), Lost Kingdom tier-ups (earned from dead and severely wounded units) **raise the return rate**, and since **1.0.89** (Dec 2024) the Hall also **refunds part of the resources spent healing** in the Lost Kingdom [A08-0601].

**No official percentage exists.** A 2022 guide says half of the lost troops come back; since 1.0.94 the rate depends on the Lost Kingdom tier, so do **not** plan with a flat 50% [A08-0602, weak card].

**What to do:** fight in the Lost Kingdom when your alliance needs you; dead troops there are partly recoverable, and the refund also covers part of the healing bill. Read the end-of-season mail and record what came back (gap L-A08-04).
why_md: Fear of losing troops keeps many low-power players out of KvK. The official rules say part of those losses and part of the healing cost come back, which changes how costly participation really is; the exact rate is unknown, so the block gives no number.
uncertain_notes: A08-0602 (50% return, one 2022 guide) is weak and superseded by the tier-based rule since 1.0.94.

title: Season of Conquest: the seasonal levers that cut healing cost
body_md:
Official posts show Lilith addressing T5 healing cost with **season-specific** levers rather than a base-cost cut [A08-0608]:
- **Crystal technologies** that reduce T5 healing cost (SoC only) [A02-0601].
- **Seasonal strategies** in King of the Nile: Frugality (−10% healing resources) saves at most **700,000,000** resources per season, Medical Skills (+15% healing speed) at most **6,000 minutes**, Safe Return (−8% severely wounded become slightly wounded) at most **500,000** units and does not affect dead units [C04-0620].
- **Healing speedups** in the SoC Wheel of Fortune pool (1.0.92) and the Hall of Heroes refund (1.0.89) [A08-0608].
- **Recovery Potions** for Acclaim Coins (1.1.04, a pioneer in the Heroic Anthem story only) [A08-0608].

**What to do:** in an SoC story, pick the healing strategies and crystal techs early, before the big fights; the caps mean they help most for a mid-sized account and stop scaling for very large heals.
why_md: Because most of the help with healing cost exists only inside SoC stories, KvK2 and KvK3 are likely the most expensive seasons to heal in (an inference from the cards, not a stated fact). Knowing the levers and their caps lets a player choose them before they are needed.

title: Crystal technology: specialise in one unit type
body_md:
In Season of Conquest stories each governor builds a **Crystal Mine** and a **Crystal Research Center** and researches crystal technologies paid with **Crystals** (from the mine, barbarian patrols/forts, Kahar, Trial of Kau Karuak and bastion quests) [A02-0601]. The reworked tree (pioneered in 1.0.94–1.0.99, rolled out to selected stories in 1.1.02) lets you invest in your **preferred unit type** without researching unused unit techs, with Unit Capacity earlier [A02-0601].

Guides advise free and low spenders to be **selective**: invest in production (Crystals, Favor) early without maxing it, then put the rest into the military branch of your **one** main unit type [A02-0602, weak card].
why_md: A free account cannot max every branch; the rework officially rewards picking one unit type. The production-first order is guide advice from before the rework, so it is labelled uncertain.
uncertain_notes: A02-0602 (selective crystal tech priorities) is weak: guide advice partly written before the 2025 rework.

title: Between seasons: gather, keep resources in items, favour gold on T5
body_md:
For the gap before KvK2, KvK3 or SoC, guides agree to **gather continuously** (farm accounts included), keep reserves as **unopened resource items** (they cannot be plundered) and, once on T5, **prioritise gold** [A04-0604]. Lilith frames the off-season the same way in its 2024 Q&A [B01-0901].

**No stockpile target is reliable.** Only one seller guide gives numbers (at least 500M food and wood, 200M stone and 100M gold in item form), and its wording does not say whether the food and wood figure is each or combined; treat it as one seller's opinion, not a target.

There is **no daily cap** on resources received by assistance or plunder: the 200M caps announced in 1.0.49 were removed on 2021-08-04 [A04-0605], so a main account can be fed by farms without a daily limit.
why_md: Healing cost is what ends a KvK for a free account, and healing is paid in resources. Items are the safe form for a stockpile because they cannot be plundered while you are offline.

title: Universal speedups: research between seasons or healing during KvK?
split_views: Research first: one guide says F2P aiming at T5 should never use universal speedups to heal. Healing reserve: 2026 commercial guides say to keep universals for KvK healing [A04-0602].
body_md:
Sources split by goal [A04-0602, weak card]: one guide tells free accounts aiming at T5 to put **every universal speedup into research** and never into healing; 2026 commercial guides say to **reserve universal speedups for hospital healing** during KvK and to use specialised speedups first.

**A rule that respects both:** use specialised (research, healing) speedups first; spend universals on the long T5 techs between seasons, but keep enough to stay in the fights your alliance commits to. Speedups spent during Mightiest Governor or power events also earn event points.
why_md: Both views are coherent; they optimise different things (long-term tech vs staying in the current KvK). The card is weak, so the guide shows the split instead of picking a side.
uncertain_notes: A04-0602 is weak (one F2P guide vs seller-site guides).

title: Gems after VIP 10: Books of Covenant or more VIP
body_md:
After VIP 10, guides split free gems between **Books of Covenant** (for Castle 25, needed for Academy 25 and T5) and more **VIP levels** (VIP 12 = 2 and VIP 14 = 3 legendary sculptures a day), buying during **More Than Gems** [A04-0600, weak card]. In one 2022 priority list the Wheel of Fortune sits between VIP 12 and VIP 14; VIP Shop and discounted Courier Station items are only for spare gems [A04-0600].

Castle 24→25 bought only with gems costs about **50,000 gems** [A04-0601, weak card], so most free accounts mix fort books with gems.
why_md: Both uses are long-term; which comes first depends on whether T5 (books) or commander sculptures (VIP) is your bottleneck. The sources are old and partly unconfirmed, so this is shown as a low-confidence orientation.
uncertain_notes: A04-0600 (gem priorities after VIP 10, 2022–2023 text without recent confirmation) and A04-0601 (derived gem price) are weak.
